subject: MSA + Order Form: security exhibit scope matrix, pen-test notice, and sampling proposal
summary: Customer asked to align MSA security exhibit and order form language for SOC 2, pen-test notice, and sampling. Internal legal proposed 60-day notice, quarterly sampling with an 'inspection-lite' option and a timeboxed forensic access clause. Meeting scheduled to finalize redlines.
messages:
From: Ben Ross <ben.ross@alderdx.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: security@alderdx.com
Date: Sat, 11 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA / OF — security exhibit alignment (SOC 2, pen test, sampling)

Hi Dylan,

Thanks for the demo last week — Alder Diagnostics is keen to move forward but legal asked us to line up final language on the security exhibit and order form before signature. Two quick asks we want to cover:

1) Pen test notice and timing — our security team requires a minimum notice window and a named contact for staging access.
2) Audit sampling — given our scale, we prefer quarterly sampling windows rather than an open-ended inspection clause.

I attached the current MSA redline we were given and a spreadsheet with our suggested frequency bands. Can we get Redwood's proposed language for: SOC 2 attestation cadence, pen-test notification timing, and a scoped forensic/access timebox?

We'd like to get this over the finish line this month. Available for a short working call next week.

Attachments: current-msa-redline.pdf, alder-sample-bands.xlsx

Thanks,
Ben Ross\Head of Security Programs\Alder Diagnostics

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Ben Ross <ben.ross@alderdx.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 11 Apr 2026 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA / OF — security exhibit alignment (SOC 2, pen test, sampling)

Hi Ben — appreciate the clear asks. Quick read-through and a pragmatic proposal below; looping in Legal (Karthik) and Security (Laura) so we can produce redline text.

Proposal summary (high-level):
- SOC 2: Redwood provides our most recent SOC 2 Type II report; attestation frequency remains annual with commitment to notify of material changes.
- Pen test: 60-day advance notice for any external penetration test; a single staged access window per year by default, with an option for an additional mutually-agreed window.
- Sampling / inspection: propose "quarterly sampling" (one 3–5 day inspection window per quarter) or alternatively an "inspection-lite" option limited to document/evidence review only.
- Forensic access: strictly timeboxed (maximum 48–72 hours per incident) and scoped to the affected systems; access requires a joint schedule and guarded read-only options where possible.

Before I draft redline language, can you confirm: staging IP whitelist process (we prefer key-based access + ephemeral creds), and whether Alder will accept the inspection-lite option as a fallback?

I can draft tracked changes by Monday if that works. If yes, let's schedule a 30-minute working session — I put a tentative slot on my calendar here: https://cal.com/redwood-security/30

Best,
Dylan Brooks\Head of Sales, Large Accounts\Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Ben Ross <ben.ross@alderdx.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, olga_petrov@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 12 Apr 2026 21:22:00 +0100
Subject: Re: MSA / OF — security exhibit alignment (SOC 2, pen test, sampling)

Ben / Dylan — thanks for the context. I reviewed the attached MSA redline and Alder's sample bands. A few legal-focused recommendations to accelerate finalization:

1) Pen test notification: 60 days is reasonable. Add a clause that requires coordination through a named security contact and includes a defined scope document (no broad unrestricted testing). Limit testing to non-production unless mutually agreed.

2) Forensic / inspection access: make this timeboxed and role-limited. Suggested language: "Forensic access will be scoped to the implicated services, delivered within a mutually-agreed time window not to exceed 72 hours per incident, barring court order or lawful process." That addresses Alder's operational needs while protecting customer data.

3) Sampling frequency: we can accept quarterly sampling if we include an 'inspection-lite' alternative for customers who prefer document/evidence-only reviews. Add an order-form toggle for "Inspection Intensity: Full | Lite" to simplify procurement and signal cost/ops impact.

4) SOC 2: Redwood will provide the latest SOC 2 Type II and a summary of deviation/controls changes within 10 business days of identification. We prefer not to commit to on-demand re-attestations — keep attestation annual.

5) Limit evidence scope and SLA for responses: propose a 10-business-day turnaround for routine evidence requests; for deeper requests (logs, packet captures) provide a separate SOW or fee schedule.

I will draft tracked-change language for the security exhibit and a short order-form clause for the inspection intensity toggle. Laura / Olga — can you confirm operational feasibility of quarterly windows and the 72-hour forensic cap?

Karthik Iyer\Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Ross <ben.ross@alderdx.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: security@alderdx.com
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2026 18:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA / OF — security exhibit alignment (SOC 2, pen test, sampling)

Dylan / Karthik — thanks, that framework looks sensible. A couple clarifications from our security ops:

- We can accept 60-day notice for external pen tests.
- Staging IPs: we will provide a CIDR block and can do ephemeral creds for engineers; key-based access preferred.
- Quarterly sampling is acceptable if the Order Form exposes the "Inspection Intensity" toggle. Alder will probably select "Lite" for initial year; we reserve the right to escalate to Full if an incident warrants.

Let's take the proposed tracked changes and walk through them — I'm good for a 30-minute call on Tuesday 13 Apr 2026 at 15:00 PDT. I've attached the spreadsheet we referenced with sample bands.

Attachments: alder-sample-bands.xlsx

Ben
Head of Security Programs\Alder Diagnostics

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, olga_petrov@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2026 09:00:00 -0700
Subject: Internal — Alder Diagnostics: next steps and owners (MSA security exhibit)

Team — summary and action items following Ben's note:

Decisions we have agreement on:
- Pen test notice: 60 days. Staging access via CIDR + ephemeral creds (customer will supply CIDR).
- Sampling: quarterly with "Inspection Intensity" toggle on the OF (Alder likely selects Lite Y1).
- Forensic access: timeboxed to max 72 hours per incident; scope-limited.
- SOC 2: annual attestation provided; notify of material deviations within 10 business days.

Action items / owners:
- Karthik: prepare tracked-change security exhibit + short OF clause (Due: Mon 19 Apr).
- Laura: confirm operational runbook for quarterly windows and one staged pen-test window (Due: Thu 15 Apr).
- Olga: draft evidence request SLA (10 business days) and sample response templates (Due: Thu 15 Apr).
- Dylan: schedule working call and send tracking link (Done — meeting 2026-04-13T22:00:00Z on cal.com).

Attachments to share with Alder in advance: proposed-security-matrix.xlsx, current-msa-redline.pdf (attached to this thread).

If anyone sees a risk with the 72-hour cap or the inspection-lite option, flag now — otherwise I'll share Karthik's redline with Alder once it's ready.

Thanks,
Dylan
